title: Woman who went viral in Albuquerque road rage case to remain behind bars - NewsBreak
text:
By Junko Featherston ,
1 days ago
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – An Albuquerque mother who went viral for smashing another driver's window with a baseball bat in front of her kids will remain behind bars.
Story continues below
Witness video captured the suspect, Jenipher Lewis, getting out of her car and taking a bat to the back window of a white pickup truck in the middle of a busy Albuquerque intersection last week. The incident happened at Wyoming and Constitution.
According to police, Lewis used a bat to break the back windshield of a truck driven by an unknown driver. A few seconds later, the driver in the white pickup sped after Lewis, ramming into the back of Lewis’ car. While both drivers took off from the scene, police eventually caught up with Lewis and found out that her two children were inside the backseat of her car when the road rage unfolded.
Lewis told police the situation spiraled after the truck pulled out of a parking lot in front of her. According to court documents, Lewis yelled at the driver and then grabbed the bat after he laughed at her. In court on Tuesday, Judge Bruce Fox said Lewis has no control over her actions and is a danger to herself, her children and the public.
"It appears the defendant has a temper, and whether she sees red or I’m not sure what the circumstances are, but she has, particularly in this case, demonstrated that there is a concern she cannot control herself if she gets upset regardless of whether if she's driving with her kids in the car or any other circumstances,” said Judge Fox.
Lewis is facing multiple charges, including child abuse and reckless driving. Police are still searching for the driver of the white pickup truck, which did not have a license plate.
